title: Which bag did it come from?
subject: draws from bag A
question: You pick either bag with equal probability and draw a red ball. What is the probability you picked bag A?
note: Bag A contains 80% red balls. Bag B contains 20% red balls.

followUp.label: a second red ball, after the first goes back
followUp.question: The ball goes back in the bag. You draw red again. What is the probability you picked bag A?
followUp.independence: Given which bag you picked, the second draw does not depend on the first. Two reds are still more likely together, because both are more likely from bag A.

title: An alert in your inbox
subject: spam messages
question: A message is marked as spam. What is the probability it really is spam?
note: The filter catches 90% of spam and incorrectly flags 10% of legitimate messages.

title: A signal worth following?
subject: undervalued assets
question: An asset is flagged. What is the probability it is undervalued?
note: All numbers are fictional. The signal flags some fairly valued assets too.

followUp.label: also flagged by a second research signal
followUp.question: A second signal flags the same asset. What is the probability it is undervalued now?
followUp.independence: Given whether the asset is undervalued, the second signal does not depend on the first. The flags still move together in the sample, because both are more common for undervalued assets.

title: The stronger filter
subject: undervalued assets
question: An asset passes the stricter filter. What is the probability it is undervalued?
note: A low false-positive rate can matter more than finding every positive case.

title: The rare-event trap
subject: faulty components
question: A component is flagged. What is the probability it is faulty?
note: Only 1% of components are faulty. A reliable inspection can still produce many false alarms.

title: A noisy regime detector
subject: high-volatility days
question: The detector flags today. What is the probability it is a high-volatility day?
note: This is a fictional classification exercise, not a forecast using market data.

title: A rare payment alert
subject: fraudulent payments
question: Observed evidence: flagged by a payment monitor. What is the probability that the case belongs to the target group (fraudulent payments)?
note: All rates are fictional. Rare fraud can still be outnumbered by false alarms.

title: Two production lines
subject: items from line A
question: Observed evidence: fails inspection. What is the probability that the case belongs to the target group (items from line A)?
note: All rates are fictional. A failed inspection gives evidence about which line produced an item.

title: Should you pack an umbrella?
subject: rainy days
question: Observed evidence: forecast says rain. What is the probability that the case belongs to the target group (rainy days)?
note: All rates are fictional. A forecast hit rate is not the probability of rain given a forecast.

title: An earnings surprise signal
subject: positive-surprise reports
question: Observed evidence: research predicts a positive surprise. What is the probability that the case belongs to the target group (positive-surprise reports)?
note: All rates are fictional. This estimates a reporting outcome, not a profitable trade after costs.

title: Detecting thin liquidity
subject: thin-liquidity intervals
question: Observed evidence: spread alarm activates. What is the probability that the case belongs to the target group (thin-liquidity intervals)?
note: All rates are fictional. The base rate applies to intervals, not the number of trades.

title: A reassuring result
subject: faulty sensors
question: Observed evidence: passes inspection. What is the probability that the case belongs to the target group (faulty sensors)?
note: All rates are fictional. Here the observed evidence is a pass: use the probability of passing in each group.

title: A signal with no information
subject: up days
question: Observed evidence: indicator turns blue. What is the probability that the case belongs to the target group (up days)?
note: All rates are fictional. Equal likelihoods leave the prior unchanged.

title: When a flag lowers your belief
subject: strong businesses
question: Observed evidence: a warning appears. What is the probability that the case belongs to the target group (strong businesses)?
note: All rates are fictional. Evidence can lower the probability of the target group.

title: A screening exercise
subject: qualified applicants
question: Observed evidence: passes a screening exercise. What is the probability that the case belongs to the target group (qualified applicants)?
note: All rates are fictional. This fictional screen illustrates selection and base rates.

title: Which coin was chosen?
subject: draws using coin A
question: Observed evidence: coin lands heads. What is the probability that the case belongs to the target group (draws using coin A)?
note: All rates are fictional. Coin A has a 70% heads rate; coin B has a 40% heads rate.

followUp.label: an independent follow-up also supports the target
followUp.question: After this second observation, what is your updated target probability?
followUp.independence: In this fictional model, observations are independent conditional on target membership. This assumption must be checked before multiplying real-world likelihoods.

title: A rare stress regime
subject: stress days
question: Observed evidence: stress indicator fires. What is the probability that the case belongs to the target group (stress days)?
note: All rates are fictional. An 80% detection rate alone does not establish an 80% posterior.

title: Where did the late parcel start?
subject: parcels from depot A
question: Observed evidence: parcel arrives late. What is the probability that the case belongs to the target group (parcels from depot A)?
note: All rates are fictional. Late parcels are less likely from the more frequently used depot.

title: Replication evidence
subject: hypotheses with a real effect
question: Observed evidence: experiment is significant. What is the probability that the case belongs to the target group (hypotheses with a real effect)?
note: All rates are fictional. These are hypothetical operating characteristics, not empirical research success rates.

followUp.label: an independent follow-up also supports the target
followUp.question: After this second observation, what is your updated target probability?
followUp.independence: In this fictional model, observations are independent conditional on target membership. This assumption must be checked before multiplying real-world likelihoods.

title: A credit warning
subject: defaults
question: Observed evidence: warning indicator activates. What is the probability that the case belongs to the target group (defaults)?
note: All rates are fictional. A classification probability is not a complete credit decision.

title: A blue ball from a small urn
subject: draws from urn A
question: Observed evidence: a blue ball is drawn. What is the probability that the case belongs to the target group (draws from urn A)?
note: All rates are fictional. Both urns are equally likely to be selected.

title: A stock-out signal
subject: stock-out days
question: Observed evidence: inventory alarm fires. What is the probability that the case belongs to the target group (stock-out days)?
note: All rates are fictional. Count all alarm days in the denominator.

title: A balanced classification problem
subject: target cases
question: Observed evidence: classifier flags the case. What is the probability that the case belongs to the target group (target cases)?
note: All rates are fictional. With equal priors, likelihoods determine the posterior odds.

title: A weak research filter
subject: genuine opportunities
question: Observed evidence: filter flags an asset. What is the probability that the case belongs to the target group (genuine opportunities)?
note: All rates are fictional. Small likelihood differences produce modest belief updates.
